Value for money and ability to manage funding at the Whitley Award level (GBP 50,000), with priority to applicants who clearly demonstrate need

official.application_route: Register at the WFN online application portal (wfn.eformsolutions.com), complete the form with the current-year Word and Excel templates, and nominate three referees.
official.citizenship_residency: Winners are nationals of the country in which they are working - born there or having lived there long term and obtained national status.
official.international_eligibility: Open to grassroots conservation leaders based in at least one eligible country (not a World Bank High-Income Economy, with exceptions based on WFN's funding history); expatriate leaders are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Wildlife conservation projects involving communities at the grassroots level and delivering practical action founded on science; WFN does not fund pure academic research, MSc or PhD fieldwork, expeditions, start-up or pilot projects, land purchases, building construction, captive animal welfare and rehabilitation, purely economic or development projects without quantifiable conservation benefit, or government employees (applicants at government-funded universities are typically eligible).
official.duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year.
official.description: Awarded annually, Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders, providing funding to support and scale up proven, science-based solutions that deliver lasting impact for both people and nature. Winning a Whitley Award can be a transformative moment in a conservation leader's career, bringing international recognition, communications and media support, and entry to a global community of more than 230 conservation leaders across over 80 countries.
official.program_type: Charitable conservation project award (Whitley Fund for Nature)
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate in English. Total fluency is not required, but applicants must be able to communicate verbally in English without a translator, so that winners can take part fully in the Whitley Awards week involving interviews, networking events, training and media opportunities.

verification.notes: Read the Whitley Fund for Nature's own apply and eligibility pages in full on 2026-10-10; the GBP 50,000 over one year figure, the 30 October 2026 23:59 GMT deadline, the Spring 2027 London ceremony, the portal and template process, the three-referee rule and the fund/not-fund lists are confirmed as published.

applicant_utility.summary: The Whitley Award is GBP 50,000 of project funding over one year for an individual grassroots leader who is a national of the country where they work and is backed by an experienced organisation - solo operators, joint entries and nominations on someone else's behalf are all excluded. The application runs through a portal with two templates that are refreshed every year, and applications on out-of-date forms from previous years are not considered, so the current-year Word logical framework and Excel budget are mandatory. Three referees must submit their references by the deadline, and that responsibility sits with you, not with them.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career conservationists embedded in their own country's communities, working for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not-for-profit or university, with a proven ecosystem-level project ready to scale.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on WFN's published list of eligible countries and that you hold national status there
Check your project is not on the not-funded list (pure academic research, degree fieldwork, expeditions, start-ups, land or buildings, captive-animal work)
Register on the WFN portal early and save progress as you go - closing without saving loses the data
Download the current-year Word logical framework and Excel budget templates from the portal and build both around measurable indicators
Line up three referees early and confirm in writing that each will upload their reference before 30 October 2026
common_rejection_risks: Submitting on last year's Word or Excel template, which voids the application
A referee who misses the deadline, leaving the application incomplete
Applying as an expatriate, a team, a one-person operation, or on behalf of someone else
A project whose conservation outcomes cannot be measured or that looks like a pilot rather than proven work
A budget that does not demonstrate value for money at the GBP 50,000 level
document_audit: Both templates must be the current-year versions downloaded from the portal; older files are rejected
The logical framework/timeline and the budget are separate documents (Word and Excel) and both must be uploaded
Referee references are uploaded by the referees themselves, so chase them well before the deadline
alerts: The deadline is 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026 - a hard close with no stated grace period
Winners are announced at the ceremony in London in Spring 2027, and winners need to communicate verbally in English for the interviews, networking and media programme
The portal warns that closing it without saving loses your information, so save continuously while drafting
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the WFN portal, complete the online form with the current-year templates, nominate three referees who upload their references, and submit before 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026; winners are announced at the London ceremony in Spring 2027.
